title: Token-surge priority-queue starvation & asymmetric circuit-breaker tripping postmortem
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Summary: On 2026-02-18 a sustained set of long-input requests originating from a single large customer (tokenization spike with many long sequences) caused priority queue starvation in the us-west-2 serving fleet. This produced asymmetric circuit-breaker tripping in secondary regions, uneven load shedding, and a 20-minute p99 SLO breach for hosted generation endpoints. This postmortem documents the timeline, root cause, mitigations applied during the incident, and follow-up action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-02-18T09:03Z - First alerts: increased p99 latency on /v1/generate in us-west-2 (internal alert threshold breached)
2026-02-18T09:05Z - Ops routed initial traffic snapshot; automated routing policy shifted some traffic to eu-west-1 (no immediate relief)
2026-02-18T09:08Z - Control plane detected per-pool queue growth; priority queue starvation observed (high-priority small requests queued behind long-sequence requests)
2026-02-18T09:12Z - Heterogeneous model fanout began amplifying backend resource usage (long requests pinned large KV caches across GPUs)

2026-02-18T09:18Z - Circuit breakers in eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1 began tripping asymmetrically due to higher error rates on fallback variants; automatic failover policies created traffic imbalance
2026-02-18T09:25Z - Manual throttles and emergency knob (regional admission control) applied; p99 latency reduced but error rate stayed elevated for 18 minutes
2026-02-18T09:43Z - Full mitigation: token-aware admission control and temporary batch-size caps enabled; traffic normalized by 09:50Z
2026-02-18T10:10Z - Post-incident triage call; incident declared resolved and postmortem assigned
impact: SLO impact: p99 latency for /v1/generate exceeded the 500ms SLO threshold for 20 minutes in us-west-2 and eu-west-1; observed 3.9% increase in 5xx errors globally during the window. Customer-facing impact: a small number of high-volume customers saw increased tail latency and a small proportion retried resulting in duplicate requests. Internal cost: temporary spike in GPU utilization and KV cache churn.
root_cause: A combination of an unexpected tokenization pattern (many long sequences from a single tenant) and lack of token-aware admission controls caused long requests to occupy priority queues and KV cache state. This queue starvation amplified heterogeneous model fanout costs and triggered cascading circuit-breaker conditions in other regions. The control plane routing hysteresis then routed additional traffic into partially degraded regions, creating asymmetric load and prolonged SLO misses.
contributing_factors: No token-length based admission control or per-tenant token caps in the priority queue
KV cache warming behavior pinned large state to a subset of GPUs, increasing load variance
Circuit-breaker cooldowns and hysteresis settings were conservative for some regions, causing slow recovery
Routing policy favored capacity-based routing without factoring recent queue-length dynamics
Lack of early per-tenant telemetry surfaced in dashboards (we lacked token-distribution time-series)
mitigation: Emergency: applied manual regional admission throttles and capped max batch size for affected pools
Enabled temporary token-aware request admission in us-west-2 to prioritize short requests
Reduced circuit-breaker strictness for fallback variants to avoid over-tripping during asymmetric degradations
Disabled aggressive routing failback for 10 minutes to let overloaded regions recover without receiving more traffic
long_term_actions: AI-1: Implement token-aware admission controller in the serving runtime (per-tenant token caps + short-request fast-lane); owner: SRE-Team; due: 2026-04-15
AI-2: Introduce per-tenant token-length telemetry and dashboarding (histograms by minute) so we can detect token spikes earlier; owner: Observability; due: 2026-03-31
AI-3: Rework KV cache eviction/warmup to avoid long-request pinning (cold-eviction policy + warmup staging); owner: Runtime; due: 2026-05-01
AI-4: Adjust circuit-breaker cooldown and hysteresis to include recent queue-length slope and cross-region health; owner: Inference Reliability; due: 2026-04-01
AI-5: Add routing policy guard to prevent routing loops and stop routing into a region with sustained queue growth for >5 minutes; owner: Control Plane; due: 2026-03-20
AI-6: Create runbook entry and automated playbook for token-surge incidents (steps, dashboards, emergency knobs); owner: SRE; due: 2026-03-10
